entries.note: Single-section Basic Law passed by the 25th Knesset on 13 July 2026 (Wikisource signature line and Hebrew Wikipedia's Basic Laws table agree). No Nevo page for the enacted law was found (only the bill, law04/24_lst_599336.htm); no archive capture of Knesset PDF 25_lsr_14112739. The Wikisource and Wikipedia lists of Basic Laws show no other enacted Basic Law outside the assigned list and the seven covered by other readers.

ordinary_statute_amendments.effect: Companion transitional law to Basic Law: The State Economy (repeals ss. 5–6 of the Law and Administration Ordinance; saving provisions). Does not alter the Basic Law's text.

Disapplied the deadline clause of s. 3(b)(1) of Basic Law: The State Economy ('but not later than...') for the 1985 budget bill. Wikisource lists it in the Basic Law's history and tags s. 3 'תיקון: תשמ״ה'; Nevo's amendments table omits it.

ordinary_statute_amendments.law: חוק מבקר המדינה (הוראות מעבר), התשמ״ח–1988, s. 3
ordinary_statute_amendments.effect: Amended s. 5 (audit) of Basic Law: The State Economy. Nevo counts it as State Economy 'Amendment No. 3'; Wikisource lists it without a number.

ordinary_statute_amendments.gazette: ס״ח תשנ״א, עמ' 30 (Wikisource's own page) / עמ' 31 (Wikisource's State Economy history); passed 12 December 1990
ordinary_statute_amendments.effect: Provided that notwithstanding s. 3(a)(2) of Basic Law: The State Economy the 1991 budget would cover nine months (change of fiscal year). Wikisource lists it in the Basic Law's history; Nevo's amendments table omits it.
Companion transitional law to Basic Law: The Judiciary (existing courts deemed established under it; consequential repeals in the Courts Law and Judges Law). Does not alter the Basic Law's text.

Indirectly amended s. 14 of Basic Law: The Judiciary (suspension of a judge also when a criminal investigation is opened). Counted by the Knesset as the Judiciary law's Amendment No. 1, which is why the 2002 amendment is 'No. 2'.

discrepancies: State Economy: Wikisource's history lists ס״ח תשמ״ה 26 (חוק משק המדינה (הוראת שעה), 1985) and ס״ח תשנ״א 31 (חוק שנת הכספים, 1990) as affecting s. 3; Nevo's amendments table (297_001.htm) lists neither.
State Economy: Wikisource's own page for חוק שנת הכספים gives ס״ח תשנ״א 30, while its State Economy history gives 31.

State Economy: Nevo numbers amendments 3, 5, 7, 8 and 12 as indirect amendments (State Comptroller transitional law 1988; Basic Law: Government 1992 s. 58; 2010 budget Basic Law amendment s. 5; Basic Law: Government (Amendment) 2014 s. 8; Basic Law: Knesset Amendment No. 51); Wikisource lists the same laws by title without those numbers, so the two numbering sequences differ although the set of laws is the same.

State Economy: Wikisource lists the 2009 Budget Basic Law enactment (ס״ח תשס״ט 134) and the budget law's amendments 2–4 (תשע״ג 52, 70; תשע״ה 194) in the State Economy history; Nevo's State Economy table lists only the 2010 amendment (as Amendment No. 7). The budget Basic Law's own Nevo page (500_157.htm) and Wikisource agree on all five gazette references.

State Economy Amendment No. 10 / temporary provision 2020: Wikisource gives ס״ח תש״ף 16 only; Nevo gives p. 16 for the temporary provision and p. 18 for the permanent amendment (same law, same issue 2791). Likewise Amendment No. 11: Wikisource 252; Nevo 252 (amendment) and 253 (temporary provision).

Basic Law: The Judiciary, Freedom of Occupation, Human Dignity and Liberty, Referendum and Nation State: Nevo now serves these in a newer page format with no amendments table or gazette footnotes in the delivered HTML (the Nevo 'law card' pages are JavaScript-rendered and returned empty), so Wikisource's amendment lists for these five laws could be cross-checked against Nevo only by the consolidated text and its date. Nevo's State Economy and budget-law pages were in the older format and were fully cross-checked.

Judiciary Amendment No. 4: Hebrew Wikipedia says passed 27 March 2025 while the Walla article it cites is dated 26 March 2025; the gazette footnote resolves it: passed 27 March 2025 in a sitting that began 26 March 2025.
Basic Law: Torah Study (2026) appears on Wikisource and in Hebrew Wikipedia's Basic Laws table but not on Nevo as an enacted law at the time of checking.
deviations: Passage dates could not be obtained from Knesset PDFs for five entries because the Internet Archive has no capture of those files and fs.knesset.gov.il / main.knesset.gov.il are geo-blocked; Nevo's gazette PDFs return 404. Those entries carry the gazette publication date from Nevo with date_basis 'published': State Economy temporary-provision amendments (תיקון), (תיקון מס' 2), (תיקון מס' 3) of 2020, and State Economy Amendments No. 13 and No. 14 (2023).

For Basic Law: The Knesset Amendment No. 50 (2020) and Amendment No. 51 (2021) the passage dates come from Hebrew Wikipedia's amendments list (no archive capture of the Knesset PDFs); Hebrew Wikipedia was otherwise used only for count cross-checks and for gazette issue numbers/dates of four laws whose Nevo pages lack footnotes (Judiciary 1984 and 2002; Freedom of Occupation 1992, 1994, 1996, 1998).

Gazette issue numbers are not given for Human Dignity and Liberty (1992), the 2002 State Economy temporary Basic Law and Basic Law: Torah Study, because the sources reached give only the Hebrew year and page.
Nevo did not require a login; pages were fetched directly. The Nevo page for the 2002 temporary Basic Law was not located.

Hebrew Wikipedia's list article 'חוקי היסוד של ישראל' returned 404; the article 'חוק יסוד' (which contains the Basic Laws table) was used instead, together with Wikisource's full list of pages prefixed 'חוק-יסוד', to confirm that Torah Study (2026) is the only enacted Basic Law outside the assigned list and the seven covered by other readers.
Work was done in a scratch subfolder (downloads and text extractions only); nothing in the repository folder was read or written. About 30 tool calls were used.
